title: Iterative Topic Taxonomy Induction with LLMs: A Case Study of Electoral Advertising
abstract: arXiv:2510.15125v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Social media platforms play a pivotal role in shaping political discourse, but the scale and rapid evolution of online content make systematic analysis difficult. We introduce an end-to-end framework for inducing an interpretable topic taxonomy from unlabeled text corpora. The framework combines embedding-based clustering with iterative large language model (LLM) inference to construct a topic taxonomy without requiring predefined labels or seed topics. It first synthesizes candidate topics from document clusters and then uses the resulting taxonomy to assign consistent topic labels across clusters. We evaluate the approach through a case study of political advertising ahead of the 2024 U.S. presidential election. We use the induced taxonomy to support downstream analyses of issue prevalence, moral framing, advertising spend, and demographic exposure patterns. translated_title: 基于大语言模型的迭代式主题分类体系归纳：选举广告案例研究
translated_abstract: 社交媒体平台在塑造政治话语方面发挥着关键作用，但在线内容的规模和快速演变使得系统性分析变得困难。我们提出了一种端到端的框架，用于从无标注文本语料库中归纳出可解释的主题分类体系。该框架将基于嵌入的聚类与迭代式大语言模型（LLM）推理相结合，无需预定义标签或种子主题即可构建主题分类体系。该框架首先从文档聚类中合成候选主题，然后利用所得的分类体系在各聚类之间分配一致的主题标签。我们通过2024年美国总统大选前政治广告的案例研究对该方法进行了评估。我们利用归纳出的分类体系支持了多项下游分析，包括议题流行度、道德框架、广告支出以及人口统计曝光模式。这些结果表明，迭代式分类体系构建可以提供……（原文截断）
tldr: 该论文提出了一种将嵌入聚类与迭代式大语言模型推理相结合的端到端框架，无需预定义标签即可从无标注文本中自动构建可解释的主题分类体系，并成功应用于2024年美国总统大选政治广告的多维度分析。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces an end-to-end framework combining embedding-based clustering with iterative LLM inference to automatically construct interpretable topic taxonomies from unlabeled text without predefined labels, demonstrated through a case study of electoral advertising ahead of the 2024 U.S. presidential election.
